outcome: In the untap step, before untapping, phased-in permanents with phasing phase out and phased-out permanents that phased out under that player's control phase in, simultaneously.
A phased-out permanent is treated as nonexistent (not counted, not destroyed by sweepers), and a permanent that phases out is removed from combat.
A permanent that phases in is treated as existing again.
Phasing causes no zone or control change: no zone-change triggers fire, tokens persist, and counters remain.
A continuous effect from a resolved spell or ability does not include a permanent that is phased out when the effect is generated.
A for-as-long-as effect tracking a permanent ends when it phases out, and other effects may expire while it is phased out so they no longer apply when it phases in.
Auras, Equipment and Fortifications attached to a permanent phase out with it and phase in along with it.
An object that would phase out both directly and indirectly phases out only indirectly.
A directly phased-out Aura or Equipment phases in attached to its former host if that is still in the same zone, otherwise unattached, followed by state-based actions.
Attach and unattach triggers do not fire when an attached permanent phases in or out.

note: a player leaving ends a two-player game

outcome: If the untap step is skipped, no phasing occurs that turn.
Multiple instances of phasing on one permanent make it phase out and in only once per cycle.
